t: Polynesian settlers lived where Honolulu stands by the 11th century, and the harbour, whose name means sheltered harbour, drew foreign merchant ships from 1794.
Kamehameha I held court in the area in 1809 and 1810, and in 1845 Kamehameha III made Honolulu the permanent capital of the Hawaiian Kingdom.
The monarchy was overthrown in 1893, the United States annexed Hawaii in 1898, and Honolulu became the capital of the territory and, from 1959, of the state.
dyk: Honolulu is Hawaiian for sheltered harbor or calm port, and its older name, Kou, covered the area that is now the heart of the downtown district.
ev: A settlement stands where Honolulu now stands, according to oral histories and artifacts
Captain William Brown of Great Britain is the first foreigner to sail into the harbour
Kamehameha I moves his royal court to what is now downtown Honolulu
Kamehameha III moves the permanent capital of the Hawaiian Kingdom from Lahaina to Honolulu
The Empire of Japan attacks nearby Pearl Harbor
Hawaii becomes a state and Honolulu its capital

f.founded: Oral histories and artifacts indicate a settlement where Honolulu now stands in the 11th century, made by the original Polynesian migrants to the archipelago; the city grew from a handful of homes in the early 19th century.
f.where: On the southeast coast of the island of Oʻahu, in the Pacific Ocean, beside Honolulu Harbor, in the state of Hawaii, United States.
f.known: Honolulu Harbor; the capital of the Hawaiian Kingdom from 1845; ʻIolani Palace; the overthrow of the monarchy in 1893 and annexation by the United States in 1898; the fire of 1900; the attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941; statehood in 1959
f.today: Honolulu is the capital and most populous city of the state of Hawaii and the county seat of the consolidated City and County of Honolulu.
